les-gardiens-du-temple: A herdsman in a white robe seen from behind walking with his cattle at dusk along a Sahelian river valley, a distant modern city with a white dome on the horizon.
voltaique: A young African woman in a maid's apron seen from behind on the balcony of a Riviera villa, looking at the blue Mediterranean, a carved African mask hanging on the wall beside her.
l-harmattan: A dusty harmattan wind sweeping a West African town square in 1958, a crowd seen from afar gathered around a wooden ballot box under a mango tree.
vehi-ciosane-suivi-du-mandat: An old man in a white boubou seen from behind waiting in a long queue at the arched doorway of a plain ochre colonial building in Dakar, holding a blue envelope, blank walls without any sign.
le-dernier-de-l-empire: An empty presidential armchair in a grand palace hall, tall windows with curtains blowing in the wind, small soldier silhouettes far away in the courtyard.
niiwam-suivi-de-taaw: A thin man seen from behind carrying a small bundle wrapped in white cloth on a crowded city bus in Dakar, palm trees and buildings passing outside the windows.
guelwaar: A small Catholic church and a mosque minaret side by side in a Senegalese village, a funeral procession seen from afar on the sandy road between them.
hosties-noires: Rows of African colonial infantrymen in red caps seen from behind marching through a grey European winter landscape, barbed wire of a prison camp in the distance.
anthologie-de-la-nouvelle-poesie-negre-e: A kora and loose blank paper sheets on a wooden table, an open window onto a landscape joining African palm trees, a Madagascar rice terrace and Caribbean volcanic hills.
chants-pour-naett: A slender woman in a long indigo dress seen from afar walking alone on a beach at twilight, a thin crescent moon over the sea.
la-belle-histoire-de-leuk-le-lievre: A clever little hare standing on its hind legs in the African savanna, facing a big lion, an elephant and a hyena under a baobab tree.
nocturnes: The Senegalese coast at night under a huge full moon, palm trees, and a seated figure seen from behind playing a kora on the sand.
nation-et-voie-africaine-du-socialisme: Farmers seen from afar working green peanut fields in long rows, a new road and a round cooperative granary under a bright sun.
liberte-1-negritude-et-humanisme: An open book, a wooden African mask and a fragment of a Greek column together on a desk in warm lamplight.
les-fondements-de-l-africanite: A camel caravan crossing golden dunes to meet people in flowing boubous under a baobab at the southern edge of the Sahara, faint pyramids on the horizon.
liberte-2-nation-et-voie-africaine-du-so: A young nation seen from above like a map: a village, a harbour and a small factory linked by new roads under a rising sun.
lettres-d-hivernage: Rainy season in Senegal, heavy indigo clouds over green fields, a writing desk with a sealed envelope and a pen by an open window.
liberte-3-negritude-et-civilisation-de-l: Many hands of different skin tones holding up a large globe made of woven wax-print fabric.
elegies-majeures: A solitary figure seen from behind standing on a cliff above the ocean at sunset, wind, high waves and flights of seabirds.
la-poesie-de-l-action: Two men seen from behind sitting in armchairs and talking in a library with tall windows overlooking a tropical garden.
liberte-4-socialisme-et-planification: A dam on a Sahelian river seen from above, irrigated green fields and a small factory, rolled blueprints in the foreground.
ce-que-je-crois: An old man seen from behind walking on a beach at dawn, wooden pirogues pulled up on the sand, shells and a baobab tree.
oeuvre-poetique: A tall baobab under a starry sky, a kora and drums resting at its foot, the sea shimmering beyond.
liberte-5-le-dialogue-des-cultures: Two arched bridges of coloured paper over a river, linking an African village of round huts and a European town of stone houses.
silence-du-choeur: A Sicilian hill village of stone houses with a church bell tower, a group of young African men seen from behind sitting on a low stone wall looking over the valley.
de-purs-hommes: A sandy cemetery on the outskirts of Dakar at dusk, an opened grave among plain tombs, a lone man seen from behind standing far away by a low wall.
la-preference-nationale: A young African woman seen from behind with a suitcase in a snowy Strasbourg street lined with half-timbered houses.
ketala: An apartment interior full of personal objects gathered as if listening: a mask, a sewing machine, a bed, a mirror and a wardrobe draped with African fabrics.
inassouvies-nos-vies: A woman seen from behind at her window at night, looking at the lit windows of the apartment building across the street in a European city.
celles-qui-attendent: Two old women and two young women seen from behind on the shore of a small Senegalese island, watching a pirogue disappear on the Atlantic.
impossible-de-grandir: A dinner table set in a European apartment, and through the window a small Senegalese island village of childhood memories with a baobab.
marianne-porte-plainte: A woman seen from behind wearing a red Phrygian cap and a wax-print dress, standing on a bridge linking two riverbanks.
les-veilleurs-de-sangomar: A young widow seen from behind writing in a notebook by candlelight at night, through the window a lagoon peninsula with tall palms and pale ghostly silhouettes on the water.
de-quoi-aimer-vivre: An old man seen from behind sitting in a small wooden boat on a calm river at sunrise, flowering trees and birds on the banks.
marianne-face-aux-faussaires: A woman in a wax-print dress and a red Phrygian cap seen from behind, facing a row of masked shadowy figures holding false masks.
le-verbe-libre-ou-le-silence: A writing desk at night with an inkwell and a pen, an open bird cage and a bird flying out of the window towards the moon.
aucune-nuit-ne-sera-noire: An old fisherman and a little girl seen from behind in a pirogue on the mangrove channels of the Saloum delta at night, under a sky full of stars.
le-temps-de-tamango: An old sailing slave ship on the horizon of a stormy sea, and in the foreground a 1970s Dakar street with a crowd of protesters seen from afar.
les-tambours-de-la-memoire: Tall drums in a sacred forest clearing in Casamance, a young man seen from behind walking towards a distant village among rice paddies.
les-traces-de-la-meute: A small village at night under the shadow of a giant mythical beast stretching over the rooftops, paw prints of a pack crossing the sand.
le-cavalier-et-son-ombre: A solitary traveller seen from behind on a river bank waiting for a ferry, a wooden boat and a ferryman on the misty river.
negrophobie: A broken mirror on a dark table reflecting a distorted shape of the African continent, shards scattered around.
kaveena: A dark villa garden in a tropical capital during a civil war, one lit window, smoke rising in the distance, an empty child's swing.
l-afrique-au-dela-du-miroir: A large ornate standing mirror in the savanna, reflecting a vibrant African coastal city and the sea beyond.
les-petits-de-la-guenon: An old man seen from behind writing in a notebook in a Senegalese courtyard, a family of small monkeys playing on the roof.
la-gloire-des-imposteurs: The Niger river with pirogues and Sahel cliffs at sunset, two letters carried by birds, small military helicopters far in the sky.
